question_text: Which layer in the dicot root prevents water loss and has casparian strips?
explanation:
The endodermis contains Casparian strips that prevent the passive movement of water, regulating transport
              into the vascular tissue.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: What differentiates an isobilateral leaf from a dorsiventral leaf?

options.text:
(1)
Presence of palisade and spongy mesophyll

explanation:
Isobilateral leaves (e.g., monocots) have stomata on both surfaces, whereas dorsiventral leaves (e.g.,
              dicots) have stomata mostly on the lower surface.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about stomatal apparatus is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Stomatal pores are surrounded by specialized guard cells.

(2)
Guard cells do not contain chloroplasts.

(3)
Subsidiary cells are always absent in the stomatal complex.

(4)
Stomata are present only in stems and absent in leaves.

explanation:
Stomata are surrounded by specialized guard cells, which regulate the opening and closing of the stomatal
              pore.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which type of simple permanent tissue provides mechanical support in mature plants?
explanation: Sclerenchyma consists of thick-walled, lignified cells that provide mechanical support in mature plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: In monocot stems, the vascular bundles are surrounded by which type of supportive tissue?
explanation:
In monocot stems, each vascular bundle is surrounded by a sheath of sclerenchyma, which provides
              mechanical support.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about the hypodermis in monocot stems is incorrect?

options.text:
(3)
It is present just below the epidermis.

explanation:
The hypodermis in monocot stems is made of sclerenchyma, whereas in dicot stems, it is made of
              collenchyma.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: What is the function of bulliform cells in monocot leaves?
explanation: Bulliform cells help in folding the leaves to reduce water loss under drought conditions.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following plant tissues is responsible for the transport of food?
explanation:
Phloem is responsible for transporting organic nutrients, primarily sucrose, from source to sink in
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which of the following statements about collenchyma is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Collenchyma provides mechanical support to young stems and leaves.

(2)
Collenchyma cells have unevenly thickened cell walls.

(3)
Collenchyma cells are dead at maturity.

(4)
Collenchyma contains pectin and cellulose in its cell walls.

explanation:
Collenchyma cells remain living at maturity and provide flexibility and mechanical support to growing
              plant parts.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which characteristic feature of dicot roots helps in selective absorption of water?
explanation:
The endodermis in dicot roots contains Casparian strips, which regulate selective water absorption into
              the vascular bundle.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 1

question_text: Which layer of cells in a dicot root lies just inside the endodermis?
explanation:
The pericycle is the layer of cells located just inside the endodermis and is responsible for the
              initiation of lateral roots.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about epidermis in plants is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
The epidermis is usually a single layer of cells.

(3)
The epidermis helps in reducing water loss.

(4)
Trichomes are part of the epidermal tissue system.

explanation: Epidermal cells generally lack chloroplasts, except for guard cells, which regulate stomatal opening.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which cells in the vascular bundle provide structural support?
explanation: Sclerenchyma fibers in vascular bundles provide mechanical strength and support to plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about xylem parenchyma is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Xylem parenchyma is dead at maturity.

(2)
Xylem parenchyma stores food and helps in lateral conduction of water.

(3)
Xylem parenchyma is responsible for the conduction of water.

(4)
Xylem parenchyma is composed of lignified dead cells.

explanation:
Xylem parenchyma consists of living cells that store starch and fats and assist in lateral water
              conduction.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which type of plant cells provide flexibility to young stems and leaves?
explanation: Collenchyma cells provide flexibility and mechanical support to young stems and leaves.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about sieve tube elements in phloem is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Sieve tube elements have nuclei at maturity.

(2)
Sieve tube elements are supported by companion cells.

(3)
Sieve tube elements are responsible for water transport.

(4)
Sieve tube elements have thick, lignified walls.

explanation: Sieve tube elements lack nuclei and depend on companion cells for their function in transporting food.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: What is the function of the casparian strip in the endodermis of roots?
explanation:
The casparian strip prevents passive movement of water and minerals, forcing selective absorption through
              plasma membranes.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about root hairs is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Root hairs develop from the endodermis.

(2)
Root hairs increase the surface area for absorption of water and minerals.

(4)
Root hairs are responsible for the transport of organic nutrients.

explanation:
Root hairs are extensions of epidermal cells that increase the surface area for absorption of water and
              minerals.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: What is the function of guard cells in stomata?

options.text:
(2)
Opening and closing of stomatal pore

explanation: Guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomatal pores to control transpiration and gas exchange.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which of the following statements about bundle sheath cells is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Bundle sheath cells surround vascular bundles.

(2)
Bundle sheath cells regulate the movement of substances into and out of vascular tissues.

(3)
Bundle sheath cells are present only in monocots.

(4)
Bundle sheath cells provide mechanical support.

explanation:
Bundle sheath cells are present in both monocots and dicots, although they are more specialized in C4
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 2

question_text: Which simple tissue in plants is responsible for photosynthesis in leaves?
explanation: Parenchyma in leaves contains chloroplasts and is called mesophyll, which carries out photosynthesis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Sclerenchyma provides mechanical support to plants.

(2)
Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity.

(3)
Sclerenchyma cells have thin cellulose walls.

explanation: Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified walls that provide strength and rigidity to plant structures.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: What is the main function of phloem in vascular plants?
explanation: Phloem transports organic nutrients like sucrose from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about casparian strips in endodermis is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Casparian strips prevent passive water flow.

(2)
Casparian strips regulate water movement into the vascular bundle.

(3)
Casparian strips are made up of suberin.

(4)
Casparian strips are found in phloem.

explanation:
Casparian strips are found in the endodermis, not in phloem, and they regulate the entry of water and
              solutes into vascular tissue.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: What is the main function of trichomes in the shoot system?
explanation: Trichomes reduce water loss by minimizing transpiration and can also provide protection.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about xylem vessels is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Xylem vessels are dead at maturity.

(2)
Xylem vessels help in the transport of water and minerals.

(3)
Xylem vessels are living at maturity.

explanation:
Xylem vessels are dead at maturity and function in conducting water and minerals from roots to other
              plant parts.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which part of the root stores starch and other nutrients?
explanation: The cortex of roots is responsible for storing starch and other nutrients.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about intercalary meristem is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Intercalary meristem is found in grasses and bamboo.

(2)
Intercalary meristem helps in elongation of internodes.

(3)
Intercalary meristem is located at the tip of the root and shoot.

(4)
Intercalary meristem is a type of primary meristem.

explanation:
Intercalary meristem is located at the base of leaves and internodes, not at the tips of roots and
              shoots.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: What is the primary function of the pericycle in dicot roots?
explanation:
The pericycle in dicot roots plays a crucial role in the initiation of lateral roots and secondary
              growth.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which of the following statements about phloem loading is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Phloem loading refers to the movement of sucrose into sieve tube elements.

(2)
Phloem loading occurs actively through companion cells.

(3)
Phloem loading is dependent on ATP.

(4)
Phloem loading occurs primarily through xylem vessels.

explanation: Phloem loading occurs via sieve tube elements and companion cells, not through xylem vessels.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 3

question_text: Which vascular tissue transports food in plants?
explanation:
Phloem is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, particularly sucrose, from the leaves to
              different parts of the plant.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and provide mechanical support.

(2)
Sclerenchyma cells remain alive at maturity.

(3)
Sclerenchyma is mainly responsible for photosynthesis.

(4)
Sclerenchyma has thin primary walls with intercellular spaces.

explanation:
Sclerenchyma consists of dead cells with thick lignified walls, providing mechanical support to the
              plant.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which part of a dicot stem contains the starch sheath?
explanation: In dicot stems, the endodermis is rich in starch grains and is known as the starch sheath.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about the endodermis in dicot roots is correct?

options.text:
(1)
It is the outermost layer of the root.

(2)
It consists of loosely arranged cells with intercellular spaces.

(3)
It contains Casparian strips, which regulate water movement.

(4)
It is made up of dead cells.

explanation: The endodermis has Casparian strips, which prevent passive water flow and regulate selective absorption.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which cells are responsible for opening and closing of stomata?
explanation: Guard cells control the opening and closing of stomata by regulating turgor pressure.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about trichomes is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Trichomes are found on roots and help in absorption.

(2)
Trichomes help in reducing water loss from aerial parts.

(3)
Trichomes are present in xylem and help in conduction.

(4)
Trichomes are involved in transport of organic nutrients.

explanation:
Trichomes are epidermal outgrowths that help in reducing transpiration and protecting the plant from
              herbivores.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which type of vascular bundle is found in monocot roots?
explanation:
Monocot roots have radial, polyarch vascular bundles, meaning they have multiple xylem bundles arranged
              radially.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which type of simple permanent tissue stores food and is involved in photosynthesis?
explanation:
Parenchyma is responsible for food storage and, when containing chloroplasts, participates in
              photosynthesis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which type of plant tissue is present in the pericycle and contributes to lateral root formation?
explanation: Parenchyma in the pericycle contributes to the formation of lateral roots in dicot plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about the cortex in roots is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The cortex is composed of lignified dead cells.

(2)
The cortex helps in water and nutrient storage.

(4)
The cortex is the innermost layer of the root.

explanation: The cortex consists of parenchymatous cells and stores water, nutrients, and starch in roots.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 4

question_text: Which of the following statements about trichomes is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Trichomes are found on roots and help in absorption.

(2)
Trichomes help in reducing water loss from aerial parts.

(3)
Trichomes are present in xylem and help in conduction.

(4)
Trichomes are involved in transport of organic nutrients.

explanation:
Trichomes are epidermal outgrowths that help in reducing transpiration and protecting the plant from
              herbivores.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following is the main function of the epidermis in plants?
explanation: The epidermis forms the outermost protective layer of the plant body and prevents excessive water loss.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: What is the main function of trichomes in the shoot system?
explanation: Trichomes reduce water loss by minimizing transpiration and can also provide protection.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and provide mechanical support.

(2)
Sclerenchyma cells remain alive at maturity.

(3)
Sclerenchyma is mainly responsible for photosynthesis.

(4)
Sclerenchyma has thin primary walls with intercellular spaces.

explanation:
Sclerenchyma consists of dead cells with thick lignified walls, providing mechanical support to the
              plant.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: What is the function of bundle sheath cells in vascular bundles?
explanation: Bundle sheath cells in vascular bundles provide mechanical support to vascular tissues.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about the epidermis in plants is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The epidermis is a single layer of cells that provides protection.

(2)
The epidermis consists of loosely packed cells with large intercellular spaces.

(3)
The epidermis is mainly responsible for transport of water and nutrients.

(4)
The epidermis in leaves lacks stomata.

explanation:
The epidermis is a protective layer made of closely packed cells, which reduces water loss and protects
              internal tissues.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about xylem is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Xylem transports water and minerals from roots to shoots.

(2)
Tracheids and vessels are the conducting elements of xylem.

(3)
Xylem fibers are responsible for conduction.

(4)
Xylem is a complex tissue composed of different cell types.

explanation: Xylem fibers provide mechanical support, while conduction of water is performed by tracheids and vessels.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following statements about the hypodermis in monocot stems is incorrect?

options.text:
(3)
It is present just below the epidermis.

explanation:
The hypodermis in monocot stems is made of sclerenchyma, whereas in dicot stems, it is made of
              collenchyma.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: What is the primary function of the endodermis in roots?
explanation:
The endodermis has Casparian strips, which regulate the movement of water and minerals into the vascular
              tissue.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which of the following plant tissues is responsible for the transport of food?
explanation:
Phloem is responsible for transporting organic nutrients, primarily sucrose, from source to sink in
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 5

question_text: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transport of water and minerals?
explanation: Xylem is responsible for the transport of water and minerals from the roots to other parts of the plant.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about intercalary meristem is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Intercalary meristem is found in grasses and bamboo.

(2)
Intercalary meristem helps in elongation of internodes.

(3)
Intercalary meristem is located at the tip of the root and shoot.

(4)
Intercalary meristem is a type of primary meristem.

explanation:
Intercalary meristem is located at the base of leaves and internodes, not at the tips of roots and
              shoots.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which tissue system includes the epidermis, stomata, and trichomes?
explanation:
The epidermal tissue system consists of the epidermis, stomata, and trichomes, which provide protection
              and regulate gas exchange.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following tissues provides mechanical support and flexibility?

subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which type of vascular bundle arrangement is present in roots?
explanation: In roots, vascular bundles are radial, where xylem and phloem are arranged on different radii.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about bundle sheath cells is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Bundle sheath cells surround vascular bundles.

(2)
Bundle sheath cells regulate the movement of substances into and out of vascular tissues.

(3)
Bundle sheath cells are present only in monocots.

(4)
Bundle sheath cells provide mechanical support.

explanation:
Bundle sheath cells are present in both monocots and dicots, although they are more specialized in C4
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about dicot leaves is incorrect?

options.text:
(2)
Dicot leaves have differentiated palisade and spongy mesophyll.

(4)
Vascular bundles in dicot leaves are arranged in a branching pattern.

explanation: Dicot leaves have stomata, primarily on the lower epidermis, for gas exchange and transpiration.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about epidermis in plants is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
The epidermis is usually a single layer of cells.

(3)
The epidermis helps in reducing water loss.

(4)
Trichomes are part of the epidermal tissue system.

explanation: Epidermal cells generally lack chloroplasts, except for guard cells, which regulate stomatal opening.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Sclerenchyma cells are living at maturity

(2)
Sclerenchyma provides flexibility to plant organs

(3)
Sclerenchyma consists of thick-walled, dead cells

Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified walls and are dead at maturity, providing mechanical strength to
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about stomata is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Each stoma is surrounded by guard cells.

(2)
Stomata are absent in leaves and present only in stems.

(3)
The outer walls of guard cells are thick, and the inner walls are thin.

Each stoma is surrounded by two guard cells, which regulate its opening and closing. The outer walls are
              thin, and the inner walls are thick.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 6

question_text: Which of the following statements about phloem is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Phloem transports food from source to sink.

(2)
Sieve tube elements have companion cells to support their function.

Phloem does not contain xylem vessels; instead, it consists of sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem
              fibers, and phloem parenchyma.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which type of simple permanent tissue makes up the majority of the cortex in dicot roots?
explanation:
The cortex of dicot roots consists mostly of parenchymatous cells, which store food and provide
              structural support.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: What is the primary function of the pericycle in dicot roots?
explanation:
The pericycle in dicot roots plays a crucial role in the initiation of lateral roots and secondary
              growth.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which type of plant tissue consists of actively dividing cells?
explanation: Meristematic tissue consists of actively dividing cells that contribute to plant growth.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which cells in the vascular bundle provide structural support?
explanation: Sclerenchyma fibers in vascular bundles provide mechanical strength and support to plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which structure in dicot stems lies between the vascular bundles and helps in lateral conduction?
explanation:
Medullary rays in dicot stems are parenchymatous cells that facilitate lateral conduction of nutrients
              and water.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which layer of the dicot stem is rich in starch grains and is also called the starch sheath?
explanation: In dicot stems, the endodermis is rich in starch grains and is referred to as the starch sheath.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which characteristic differentiates monocot stems from dicot stems?
explanation:
Monocot stems have vascular bundles scattered throughout the ground tissue, unlike dicot stems, which
              have a ring arrangement.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which layer of the root is directly responsible for the absorption of water and minerals?
explanation: The epidermis, especially its root hairs, absorbs water and minerals from the soil.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: Which of the following statements about xylem vessels is incorrect?

Xylem vessels are dead at maturity.

Xylem vessels help in the transport of water and minerals.

Xylem vessels are living at maturity.

Xylem vessels are dead at maturity and function in conducting water and minerals from roots to other

subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 7

question_text: What type of vascular bundle is found in leaves?

question_text: Which simple tissue in plants is responsible for photosynthesis in leaves?

subject: Biology

question_text: Which type of mesophyll tissue is responsible for maximum photosynthesis in dicot leaves?

Palisade parenchyma cells contain abundant chloroplasts and carry out most of the photosynthesis in dicot
              leaves.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 8

options.text:

It is the outermost layer of the root.

It consists of loosely arranged cells with intercellular spaces.

(3)
It contains Casparian strips, which regulate water movement.

It is made up of dead cells.

explanation: The endodermis has Casparian strips, which prevent passive water flow and regulate selective absorption.
subject: Biology

question_text: Which of the following statements about sclerenchyma is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
Sclerenchyma provides mechanical support to plants.

Sclerenchyma cells are dead at maturity.

(3)
Sclerenchyma cells have thin cellulose walls.

explanation: Sclerenchyma cells have thick, lignified walls that provide strength and rigidity to plant structures.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about the epidermal tissue system is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The epidermis is usually single-layered and protects the plant.

Epidermal cells are dead at maturity and have thick walls.

Stomata are present in roots for gaseous exchange.

The cuticle is present in all plant organs, including roots.

The epidermis is a single-layered protective layer in plants. It is made up of living cells, and the

source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which part of the dicot stem lies between the vascular bundles and functions in lateral conduction?

Casparian strips prevent passive water flow.

(3)
Casparian strips are made up of suberin.

(4)
Casparian strips are found in phloem.

explanation:
Casparian strips are found in the endodermis, not in phloem, and they regulate the entry of water and
              solutes into vascular tissue.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which cells in the leaves help in minimizing water loss by curling under dry conditions?
explanation:
Bulliform cells help in minimizing water loss by causing the leaf to curl inward under water stress
              conditions.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: Which of the following statements about companion cells in phloem is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Companion cells are dead at maturity.

(2)
Companion cells help in the functioning of sieve tube elements.

(3)
Companion cells transport water and minerals.

(4)
Companion cells have thick, lignified walls.

explanation:
Companion cells are living cells that help regulate the function of sieve tube elements in transporting
              organic nutrients.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 8

question_text: In monocot stems, the vascular bundles are surrounded by which type of supportive tissue?
explanation:
In monocot stems, each vascular bundle is surrounded by a sheath of sclerenchyma, which provides
              mechanical support.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about bulliform cells in monocot leaves is correct?

options.text:
(1)
They are absent in monocot leaves.

(2)
They help in leaf rolling under drought conditions.

(3)
They are involved in mechanical support.

explanation: Bulliform cells help in leaf rolling during water stress, reducing water loss in monocot leaves.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which part of the root stores starch and other nutrients?
explanation: The cortex of roots is responsible for storing starch and other nutrients.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which cells are responsible for giving strength to vascular bundles in monocot stems?
explanation:
In monocot stems, each vascular bundle is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, which provides
              strength and support.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which type of ground tissue is responsible for providing mechanical support in young stems?
explanation: Collenchyma provides mechanical support to young growing stems and petioles.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about monocot leaves is incorrect?

options.text:
(2)
Bulliform cells help in leaf rolling during water stress.

(3)
Mesophyll in monocot leaves is differentiated into palisade and spongy layers.

(4)
Monocot leaves have stomata on both surfaces.

explanation:
In monocot leaves, mesophyll is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma, unlike dicot
              leaves.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about mesophyll in leaves is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Mesophyll is made up of xylem and phloem tissues.

explanation: Mesophyll contains chloroplasts and is responsible for photosynthesis in leaves.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which plant tissue is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients?
explanation:
Phloem is responsible for the transport of organic nutrients, mainly sucrose, from source to sink in
              plants.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about dicot and monocot leaves is correct?

options.text:
(3)
Dicot leaves have palisade and spongy mesophyll

(4)
Monocot leaves have a ring of vascular bundles

explanation:
Dicot leaves have distinct palisade and spongy mesophyll layers, while monocot leaves do not show this
              differentiation.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which of the following statements about the ground tissue system is incorrect?

options.text:
(1)
It includes all tissues except epidermis and vascular tissues.

(2)
It is mainly composed of parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.

(3)
It plays no role in photosynthesis.

(4)
Mesophyll in leaves is a part of the ground tissue system.

explanation:
The ground tissue system includes mesophyll, which contains chloroplasts and plays an essential role in
              photosynthesis.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 9

question_text: Which part of a plant is composed mainly of simple tissues?
explanation: The ground tissue consists mostly of simple tissues like parenchyma, collenchyma, and sclerenchyma.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about the cortex in roots is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The cortex is composed of lignified dead cells.

(2)
The cortex helps in water and nutrient storage.

(4)
The cortex is the innermost layer of the root.

explanation: The cortex consists of parenchymatous cells and stores water, nutrients, and starch in roots.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about pericycle in roots is correct?

options.text:
(1)
The pericycle is the innermost layer of the cortex.

(2)
The pericycle gives rise to lateral roots.

(3)
The pericycle is absent in dicot roots.

(4)
The pericycle is made up of xylem and phloem tissues.

explanation: The pericycle is responsible for the initiation of lateral roots in dicot and monocot roots.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which layer in dicot roots lies between the epidermis and the vascular bundle?
explanation: The cortex lies between the epidermis and vascular bundle and consists mainly of parenchymatous cells.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about stomatal apparatus is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Stomatal pores are surrounded by specialized guard cells.

(2)
Guard cells do not contain chloroplasts.

(3)
Subsidiary cells are always absent in the stomatal complex.

(4)
Stomata are present only in stems and absent in leaves.

explanation:
Stomata are surrounded by specialized guard cells, which regulate the opening and closing of the stomatal
              pore.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following statements about endodermis in roots is correct?

options.text:
(1)
Endodermis is the outermost layer of the root.

(3)
Endodermis is made up of dead cells.

(4)
Endodermis stores starch in monocot roots.

explanation:
Endodermis cells contain Casparian strips, which help regulate the movement of water and solutes into the
              vascular bundle.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which of the following structures is unique to monocot leaves?
explanation:
Bulliform cells in monocot leaves help in minimizing water loss by curling the leaves under drought
              conditions.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which vascular tissue component provides structural support in plants?
explanation:
Tracheids are elongated, lignified cells in xylem that provide structural support and facilitate water
              conduction.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: What is the main function of phloem in vascular plants?
explanation: Phloem transports organic nutrients like sucrose from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10

question_text: Which layer in the dicot root prevents water loss and has casparian strips?
explanation:
The endodermis contains Casparian strips that prevent the passive movement of water, regulating transport
              into the vascular tissue.
subject: Biology
source: ScienceLesson.in — Biology / Anatomy of Flowering Plants / Test 10
